A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. The expanded bibliography shifts appendix pagination without removing material.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 report original neural-emulator experiments for advection and Burgers equations. Appendix C reports additional numerical experiments and ablations.

after.justification: The original experiments in Section 4 and Appendix C are retained, including measured superiority ratios and comparisons across architectures.

M1.justification: The linear emulator formulations, neural architectures, training objectives, and autoregressive inference procedures are unchanged. The added PDE-transformer citation does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: The same advection and Burgers experiments and initial-condition scenarios are retained, alongside the same diffusion and Poisson analytical studies. Particle physics appears only as added literature context.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same neural architectures and numerical-solver comparators, including Table 5's five architectures. Neither newly cited work is added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix B retains identical model sizes, sample counts, training schedules, MSE/nRMSE metrics, spatial resolutions, and rollout horizons. Appendix C's experimental settings also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The reference-solver and rollout analyses, multimode case study, CNN receptive-field and FNO mode ablations, Picard-iteration study, and additional Burgers architecture comparison are already present in v1 and retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 12 random-seed repetitions for advection and 30 network-initialization seeds for Burgers. Existing median and percentile-interval reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported curves, numerical entries, and findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 5 retains time-step-10 superiority ratios of 0.65 for Dilated ResNet and 1.68 for Transformer.

T1.justification: The superiority definition, Fourier analyses, closed-form derivations, and supervised/discrete-residual equivalence proof are unchanged. Appendix B's Burgers solver derivation is also identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion remain unchanged. Section 6 nevertheless qualifies the novelty claim from outperforming data with significant structural errors to significant '(deterministic) structural errors', a limited refinement of its claimed scope.

C2.justification: The explanations involving inductive biases, spectral generalization, and error accumulation remain unchanged, as do the limitations concerning specific operating regimes and training-solver accuracy in Section 5.

D1.justification: Code and notebook access information, JAX/APEBench implementation details, architecture hyperparameters, optimization settings, GPU hardware, and reported runtimes are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Holzschuh et al. (2025), PDE-transformer, and Butter et al. (2021), GANplifying event samples. It acknowledges generative amplification from limited or noisy data and distinguishes the paper's deterministic structural-error setting. Both references are added to the bibliography.

P1.justification: Section 6 receives localized rewriting and paragraph reorganization. Spelling errors are corrected, and Rene Winchenbach is added to the acknowledgements. The remaining narrative and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Added text causes limited reflow on page 10 and in the bibliography, leaving the final reference on a largely empty page. All 13 figures and five tables retain their displays, captions, and placement relative to surrounding content.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves research positioning by acknowledging the related amplification phenomenon and specifying deterministic structural errors in its novelty statement. The additional context and editorial corrections improve clarity, while the scientific arguments, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
